title: India Gets Its Own Road to Esports World Cup 2026
excerpt: A new Chess.com and JioBLAST tournament gives Indian players — pros and amateurs alike — a direct shot at Riyadh.
body:
Chess and esports collided on May 11, 2026, when the Esports Foundation and JioBLAST announced 'India Rising: Road to EWC' — a national competition pathway giving Indian chess players their first official route to the Esports World Cup 2026 in Riyadh.

**What India Rising offers:**
The tournament carries a $30,000 prize fund, but the real prize is one guaranteed spot at the EWC Chess main event, scheduled from August 11 to 15. The structure blends accessibility with ambition: online qualifiers kick off May 18 for non-titled players, while a separate Indian Qualifier on May 23 targets titled players registered with the Indian federation. The two finalists then travel to Mumbai for a live, winner-takes-all grand finale on LAN.

**Why this moment matters:**
India's chess depth is extraordinary — Grandmasters Gukesh Dommaraju, Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu, Nihal Sarin, and Arjun Erigaisi headline a generation that has reshaped global rankings. Yet as Chess.com notes, Indian players are still fighting to secure their place at the next EWC through the main qualifying cycle. India Rising directly solves that problem. JioBLAST, the Jio joint venture created specifically to accelerate esports growth in India, is sponsoring the event and overseeing production, with over 10,000 grassroots players expected to enter through open qualifiers.

**What to watch next:**
With the Mumbai LAN final drawing closer and the EWC Chess event set for August 11 to 15 in Riyadh, all eyes will be on whether India Rising crowns a grassroots surprise or an established Grandmaster as the nation's esports standard-bearer.
